newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN TAX HOLIDAYS ATTRACT 13 NEW PROJECTS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN TAX HOLIDAYS ATTRACT 13 NEW PROJECTS.

text.p: Tax holiday incentives in South Africa attracted new investments worth 627 million rand by April, Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Wednesday.
He said the Department of Trade and Industry had received 13 applications for tax holidays for new investments. Six of these, valued at 59.7 million rand and creating 215 new jobs, had been approved.
Introducing the parliamentary debate on his 1997/98 budget, Erwin said the applications could create 1,432 new jobs.
"I believe that this is a relatively good start to the programme of tax holidays," he said.
Tax holidays was one of the measures announced in the macro-economic policy document last year aimed at boosting growth.
Another recent policy measure was the introduction of compensatory tariff reductions to deal with the depreciation of the rand.
"It became clear that we should look at the specific changes in currency in relation to specific sectors," Erwin said.
"It would not be accurate to take the basket of currencies and feel that this applies to all sectors."
As a result, the Board on Tariffs and Trade started sector specific studies to determine what cuts were needed.

It was also decided that the general export incentive scheme should end on July 1, which was earlier than planned, and the department was considering what concessions could be made to Southern African Development Community (SADC) countries.
"We should be prepared to make very significant market access proposals to SADC," Erwin said.
"While total trade with SADC in 1995 was 28 billion rand out of total trade of 100 billion rand, only 1,4 billion rand was imports from SADC.
"The point is obvious.If we are going to create growth and development in this sub-continent, we must allow greater access and greater investment into SADC," Erwin said
